## Functions

### `load_file_failfast`

```python
load_file_failfast(file_path: str, format: str, schema: Any | None=None, options: dict[str, Any] | None=None) -> DataFrame
```

Load a file with strict parsing and fail with corrupt-record diagnostics.

CSV, JSON, and XML are first read with Spark ``FAILFAST`` mode and
validated by an aggregate referencing every parsed field. If that read
fails, one diagnostic ``PERMISSIVE`` read counts corrupt records without
caching. The diagnostic DataFrame is never returned. Warning logs contain
at most five corrupt-row samples, each truncated to 500 characters plus
an ellipsis. Only bounded sample strings reach the Python process.

Returned DataFrames are uncached. Later actions can reread the input, so
sources must remain stable throughout validation and downstream use.
No snapshot isolation, staging storage, or new storage permissions are
provided or required.

Parquet and Delta are read and materialized once without a diagnostic
retry. The helper obtains an active Spark session or creates one and accepts
any path supported by the selected Spark data source. It adds no retry,
authentication, or timeout configuration beyond Spark and the underlying
storage connector.

Args:
    file_path: Non-empty path accepted by the Spark data source.
    format: Spark source format: ``csv``, ``json``, ``xml``,
        ``parquet``, or ``delta``.
    schema: Optional schema passed to the Spark reader.
    options: Optional Spark reader options. ``mode`` and
        ``columnNameOfCorruptRecord`` are ignored because this helper owns
        the strict read and diagnostic retry behavior.

Returns:
    Uncached, validated strict-read DataFrame for row formats, or the
    materialized Parquet or Delta DataFrame.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``file_path`` or ``format`` is missing, or the format is
        unsupported.
    FileReadError: If a row-format strict read fails and the diagnostic
        read completes.
    Exception: Propagates Spark, storage, Parquet/Delta, and diagnostic-read
        failures that are not converted to :class:`FileReadError`.
        Diagnostic failures retain their type and chain to the original
        strict-read failure. Corrupt-only inferred schemas remain subject
        to the Spark reader's restrictions.

### `load_file_stringleaf`

```python
load_file_stringleaf(file_path: str, format: str, schema: StructType, options: dict[str, Any] | None=None) -> DataFrame
```

Load a file with a shape-preserving string-leaf schema.

Struct and array shape, nullability, and field metadata are preserved.
Primitive leaves become ``StringType`` except binary leaves, which remain
binary; map key types are also preserved while map value leaves are
converted recursively.

Spark reads in ``PERMISSIVE`` mode with a corrupt-record column. For CSV,
JSON, and XML, a bounded aggregate validates every parsed field and counts
corrupt records. Parquet and Delta retain their existing count actions.
No data is cached or staged. Warning logs contain up to five corrupt-row
samples, each truncated to 500 characters plus an ellipsis. An active Spark
session is reused or a new one is created.

Later actions can reread the input. Sources must remain stable throughout
validation and downstream use; this helper provides no snapshot isolation.

Args:
    file_path: Non-empty path accepted by the Spark data source.
    format: ``csv``, ``json``, ``xml``, ``parquet``, or ``delta``.
    schema: Target structural schema used to derive the stringleaf read schema.
    options: Optional Spark reader options. ``mode`` and
        ``columnNameOfCorruptRecord`` are ignored.

Returns:
    Uncached DataFrame with the derived raw schema. A helper-added
    ``_corrupt_record`` column is dropped; a caller-declared column with
    that name is retained.

Raises:
    ValueError: If required arguments are missing, ``schema`` is not a
        ``StructType``, or ``format`` is unsupported.
    FileReadError: If Spark detects corrupt records while loading the file.
    Exception: Propagates Spark, storage, and materialization failures.

### `cast_stringleaf_to_schema`

```python
cast_stringleaf_to_schema(df: DataFrame, schema: StructType, default_date_format: str=_DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT, default_timestamp_format: str=_DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT) -> DataFrame
```

Cast a stringleaf DataFrame into the requested target schema.

Every target top-level and nested struct field must exist with the same
struct, array, and map shape and ``StringType`` scalar leaves. Extra source
fields are omitted from the result. Dates and timestamps use a non-empty
field metadata ``format`` value when present, then the corresponding
default format. Other non-string scalars use Spark ``try_cast``.

The helper runs Spark actions to count invalid rows and collect path counts.
On failure it logs path summaries and up to five compact source-row samples,
which may contain data values. Map-key conversion also rejects duplicate
keys created by casting. No retry is performed.

Args:
    df: Source DataFrame whose leaf values are strings.
    schema: Target schema to cast into.
    default_date_format: Spark date pattern used when field metadata has no
        non-empty ``format``.
    default_timestamp_format: Spark timestamp pattern used when field
        metadata has no non-empty ``format``.

Returns:
    DataFrame projected to the fields and types in ``schema``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``df`` or ``schema`` is invalid.
    FileReadError: If the source shape is incompatible, a target field is
        missing, or any non-null value cannot be converted.
    Exception: Propagates Spark analysis and execution failures.
